A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViLP benchmark and Image-DPO method. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original human and VLM evaluations, Image-DPO training results, corruption analyses, and quantitative benchmark comparisons in Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional comparator results and a Text-DPO corruption ablation.

M1.justification: Image-DPO retains the same self-generated QIA pipeline, Gaussian blur, pixelation, semantic corruption, and preference objective with fixed questions and answers. Expanded exposition and the corrected sampling index in Equation 4 do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: SEED-Bench evaluation disappears from v1 Table 4 and Section 5.1 without a replacement elsewhere. ViLP, NaturalBench, MM-Vet, CHAIR, the training seed datasets, and the appendix benchmark comparisons remain.

E2.justification: The Image-DPO comparison changes substantially: v1 Table 3 includes CSR, RLHF-V, and Text-DPO; v2 Table 4 removes CSR and adds HADPO, EOS, SIMA, and V-DPO while retaining RLHF-V and Text-DPO. These are evaluated comparator changes, not citation renumbering.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a Text-DPO control trained with corrupted images and adds the NaturalBench NB_B metric. Existing Image-DPO training settings in Appendix C.2 remain unchanged, including dataset sizes, batches, LoRA parameters, learning rate, and two training epochs.

E4.justification: V2 Section 5.1 adds an ablation testing whether corrupted-image exposure alone explains Image-DPO's advantage by training Text-DPO with the same corruption types. The distractor, image-transformation, instruction-following, and appendix benchmark analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The Whoops! comparison retains five GPT-4o attempts at temperature 1.0 and the same standard-deviation reporting in v1 Appendix D.2.2 and v2 Appendix A.3.2. No new repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice appears.

E6.justification: Although Table 2 is unchanged, the Image-DPO results are substantially revised: Cambrian's ViLPF Score changes from 11.50 to 20.83, while LLaVA-7B's MM-Vet score changes from 33.8 to 32.3. V2 adds comparator, NB_B, and corruption-ablation results and removes CSR and SEED results. Its first-place comparison uses a different comparator set; CSR previously led ViLPP with 40.84.

T1.justification: The benchmark criteria and substantive Appendix B mathematics are unchanged. V2's named Proposition 1 and proof sketch summarize the upper-bound claim and derivation already present in v1 rather than introducing a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: ViLP probes visual-language priors, current VLMs trail humans, and Image-DPO improves visual reliance through self-generated data and image corruption. The RLHF upper-bound claim also already appears in v1.

C2.justification: V2 removes the interpretation that benchmarking implicitly measures divergence between human and model priors in Section 3.1. It also changes 'stereotype-averse' to 'stereotype-consistent' responses in the Whoops! comparison and removes criticisms concerning HallusionBench's answer ambiguity and human difficulty.

D1.justification: V2 adds a stated access location for the benchmark, code, and synthetic data. Appendix A.2 changes the reported generation cost from $7.50 to $2.50 per QIA triplet, while the human-study description drops the approximately 1.5-hour session duration. Implementation prompts and training hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations concerning MIA-DPO, fine-grained AI feedback, EOS, and V-DPO, and explicitly distinguishes Image-DPO from concurrent MDPO/V-DPO approaches. It also removes the tool-use analogy and associated references. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, benchmark description, and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting and condensation. V1 Appendix D is integrated into Appendix A, the appendix contents page disappears, and a theoretical summary is brought into Section 4.1.

P2.justification: V2 adopts two-column main text and benchmark-appendix layouts, combines the existing method schematics into Figure 2a/b, rearranges and enlarges benchmark illustrations, and restructures the result tables. Numerous figures are resized or relocated; the transformation plots and generated-QIA gallery content are retained.

improvement.justification: The new corruption ablation, broader comparator set, and code/data access information strengthen evaluation and usability. However, v2 removes CSR, the strongest ViLPP comparator in v1, and SEED-Bench results, while revising several scores without explaining why despite unchanged reported training settings. These benefits and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment from the PDFs.
